run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T16:56:18Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert is firing because frontend-proxy returns HTTP 504 response_timeout (Envoy's 15 s upstream timeout) to the synthetic load generator on /api/cart and /api/checkout. The requests are not slow in the proxy: the proxy's egress spans to frontend last the same 15 s, and frontend spans that did complete carry HTTP 500 with a gRPC FAILED_PRECONDITION propagated from cart. Cart's own error spans and container logs show the underlying failure inside cart: 'Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' raised at cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected(). Cart logged 'Connection failed. Disposing the object' at 16:54:20.940Z and then 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' every few seconds until at least 17:02:54Z, and cart's Redis command spans (HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE) and successful GetCart/AddItem rates fell to zero between 16:55:18 and 16:57:18. The frontend-proxy ingress error-span rate went from ≤0.011/s to 1.31-1.46/s at 16:59-17:05 before traffic ceased, the same order as the 1.0888 value the alert carried at 16:56:18. Cart is the deepest component with its own failure evidence; the dependency valkey-cart was checked and its container shows no failure (Running/Ready, 0 restarts, no OOM, memory failcnt 0, CPU ~0.0022 cores against a 10m limit, redis metrics still scraped at 17:02:18), so why cart could no longer reach valkey-cart is not established. Candidate explanations that remain open are a cart-side network/DNS/Redis-client reachability failure, valkey-cart's very tight 10Mi memory limit (RSS 9.74 MB ≈ 93% of the limit, fragmentation ratio 5.71) degrading new-connection handling, and cart's 45m CPU limit causing CFS throttling; the last two are correlation only. Impact observed on other entities: frontend (own 500/error spans on /api/cart and /api/checkout), checkout (own CartService/GetCart and PlaceOrder error spans) and load-generator (own 504 spans). All 21 otel-demo pods, all five nodes and the CoreDNS pods looked healthy at container level when checked.

ERROR-status span increases in the window by service: frontend-proxy 961.29, frontend 256.39, cart 84.0, checkout 13.5, recommendation 3.05, ad 2.04, fraud-detection 2.04, accounting 0, payment 0.

frontend-proxy access logs record "504 UT response_timeout" with upstream times of 14,999-15,001 ms for "POST /api/cart", "GET /api/cart" and "POST /api/checkout" between 17:02:22Z and 17:02:41Z.

frontend ERROR span rate was 0 until 16:57:18Z, then 0.173/s (16:59:18Z), 0.346/s (17:01:18Z), 0.489/s (17:03:18Z), 0.578/s (17:05:18Z), 0.271/s (17:07:18Z) and 0 (17:09:18Z); frontend UNSET span rate fell from about 45/s to about 16/s.

valkey process CPU time rates were user ~0.00081-0.00146 cores and sys ~0.00059-0.00097 cores (following 0.0003 at 17:00:18Z), far below its 10m CPU limit.

10-minute ERROR-span increases at 17:12:21Z were still frontend-proxy 216.32, frontend 79.87 and cart 26.62.

frontend-proxy and load-generator container logs both end at 17:02:56Z (load-generator last line 'User browsing product: 0PUK6V6EV0' at 17:02:56.957Z; proxy last request log 17:02:56.957Z), and the CoreDNS pods coredns-b5494cbf4-48phd / coredns-b5494cbf4-z7jj2 were Running with 0 restarts when checked.

The valkey-cart container shows no sign of a crash or OOM: restartCount 0, empty lastState, container_memory_failcnt increase 0, max working set 4,284,416 bytes below the 10Mi limit, CPU ~0.0022 cores against a 10m limit — so the evidence does not support valkey being killed or restarted.

cart's Redis command spans (HGET, HMSET, EXPIRE) never carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR in this window; they simply stop being emitted, so there is no evidence that valkey returned command-level errors — the failure observed is at connection establishment.

frontend-proxy itself stayed Running/Ready with 0 restarts, its egress spans to frontend are 15 s long with http.status_code 0, and the innermost failing spans belong to cart — the 504 is a timeout on a slow upstream, not a proxy crash.

Rejected: that valkey-cart was OOM-killed or restarted and thereby broke cart storage. Its container has restartCount 0, empty lastState, memory failcnt 0 and was still exporting Redis metrics at 17:02:18Z.

Rejected: that the frontend-proxy service itself is the failing component. Its 504s are UT response_timeout at exactly ~15 s waiting on frontend, its own pod has 0 restarts, and the downstream frontend and cart spans in the same traces carry the actual errors.

Rejected as this cause: the stuck old pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s. cart's connection to valkey-cart broke at 16:54:20Z and could not be re-established for the rest of the observed window (until at least 17:02:54Z); the transport-level mechanism (DNS resolution, TCP path, or Redis handshake inside the cart pod) is not visible in the logs or traces, so this remains the leading explanation but not a proven one.

valkey-cart's very small cgroup memory allowance (RSS 9.74 MB against the 10Mi limit, fragmentation ratio 5.71) may have left it unable to service new client connections even though its existing scrape kept working; this would explain a cart-only connection failure but the evidence is indirect and no OOM occurred.

cart's 45m CPU limit and severe CFS throttling (0.62-0.86 of periods after 16:56, against 0.17-0.21 before) may have delayed or broken its Redis connect/retry path and request handling; because the throttling rose after the 16:54 onset this is correlation, not established causation.

The namespace-wide pod replacement at 16:23:06Z (new cart-755465879b, valkey-cart-58df56c79c, frontend-675fd7b5c5 and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985 ReplicaSets and pods, now carrying the small limits above) may have introduced the configuration the incident ran under; the source of that change is not visible because change_history is not integrated.

Verify from inside the cart pod whether valkey-cart resolves and accepts TCP on 6379 (DNS lookup plus a connect/INFO check) and compare that with the otel-collector redisreceiver scrape, which kept working; check the valkey process for maxclients/maxmemory and connection-refusal output, since its stdout produced no readable lines.

Review the resource limits placed on this workload — valkey-cart cpu 10m / memory 10Mi (Redis RSS 9.74 MB ≈ 93% of the limit) and cart cpu 45m (0.62-0.86 CFS throttling) — as configuration risk and raise them based on measurement, since current headroom is extremely small.

Locate the RequestErrorRate alert rule definition outside this Prometheus (it was not found here) to confirm the exact expression and window, and review the 16:23:06Z namespace-wide redeploy through a change-management source once change_history is available.

gaps: No valkey-cart application logs were returned (fetch_pod_logs for valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr returned status no_data with zero lines), and there is no exec capability, so whether valkey was listening and accepting connections at 16:54-17:02Z could not be verified.

The NetworkPolicy query for namespace otel-demo returned status no_data (no objects), so the absence of network policies could not be verified and a policy-based cause is neither confirmed nor excluded.
The transport-level reason cart could not reach valkey-cart is not recorded in any readable source; cart only logs 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' and the trace status carries no socket/DNS detail.

The alerting rule named RequestErrorRate was not found in the Prometheus rules (list_prometheus_rules rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no_data), so its expression, evaluation window and threshold are unknown.

change_history is not integrated, so it cannot be confirmed whether or why the whole otel-demo workload was redeployed at 16:23:06Z or whether the current small CPU/memory limits were introduced then.

Trace-metric series for all services stop around 17:07-17:09Z and instant queries at 17:12:21Z returned no_data; with frontend-proxy and load-generator logs ending at 17:02:56Z, the state after ~17:03Z and whether the alert resolved are unknown.

Only two Kubernetes events exist in the window, both about the old pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s at 16:59Z; when its termination began, why it was Ready in the pod listing while still emitting cadvisor series, and whether it was a cart Service endpoint during 16:23-16:59Z are unknown.
The log query for the otel-collector pod returned no readable lines, so collector-side ingestion or scrape errors during the incident are unknown.

valkey-cart's empty logs leave valkey's own view of the client connections (or of a maxmemory/maxclients condition) unverified; the conclusion that valkey stayed healthy rests on container metrics and the collector's Redis scrape only.
next_steps: Run a connectivity check from the cart pod to valkey-cart:6379 (DNS resolution plus a Redis PING/INFO) and capture the exact error, to separate DNS, TCP and Redis-handshake failure.
Inspect the valkey-cart process state (INFO clients, INFO memory, maxmemory, connected_clients, rejected_connections) and its logs, since its stdout was empty in this investigation.

Compare the current pod resource limits with the pre-16:23:06Z deployment manifests (or a GitOps/change-history record) to confirm whether the 10Mi/10m valkey limits and the 45m cart limit were introduced by that rollout.
Retrieve the RequestErrorRate alert rule from Alertmanager/Prometheus rule sources and confirm its current firing state, since the rule was not present in this Prometheus.
Query NetworkPolicies and the cart Service endpoints during the incident window from a source that returns data, since the NetworkPolicy view was no_data here.

hypothesis.text: cart's connection to valkey-cart broke at 16:54:20Z and could not be re-established for the rest of the observed window (until at least 17:02:54Z); the transport-level mechanism (DNS resolution, TCP path, or Redis handshake inside the cart pod) is not visible in the logs or traces, so this remains the leading explanation but not a proven one.

valkey-cart's very small cgroup memory allowance (RSS 9.74 MB against the 10Mi limit, fragmentation ratio 5.71) may have left it unable to service new client connections even though its existing scrape kept working; this would explain a cart-only connection failure but the evidence is indirect and no OOM occurred.

cart's 45m CPU limit and severe CFS throttling (0.62-0.86 of periods after 16:56, against 0.17-0.21 before) may have delayed or broken its Redis connect/retry path and request handling; because the throttling rose after the 16:54 onset this is correlation, not established causation.

recommendation.text: Verify from inside the cart pod whether valkey-cart resolves and accepts TCP on 6379 (DNS lookup plus a connect/INFO check) and compare that with the otel-collector redisreceiver scrape, which kept working; check the valkey process for maxclients/maxmemory and connection-refusal output, since its stdout produced no readable lines.

Review the resource limits placed on this workload — valkey-cart cpu 10m / memory 10Mi (Redis RSS 9.74 MB ≈ 93% of the limit) and cart cpu 45m (0.62-0.86 CFS throttling) — as configuration risk and raise them based on measurement, since current headroom is extremely small.

Locate the RequestErrorRate alert rule definition outside this Prometheus (it was not found here) to confirm the exact expression and window, and review the 16:23:06Z namespace-wide redeploy through a change-management source once change_history is available.

counter_evidence.text: The valkey-cart container shows no sign of a crash or OOM: restartCount 0, empty lastState, container_memory_failcnt increase 0, max working set 4,284,416 bytes below the 10Mi limit, CPU ~0.0022 cores against a 10m limit — so the evidence does not support valkey being killed or restarted.

valkey's Redis metrics were still being scraped by otel-collector at the end of the failure period (last sample 17:02:18Z, memory values stable at used 1,710,360 / rss 9,744,384), so the valkey process was alive and responsive to that scrape while cart was reporting it could not connect.

cart's Redis command spans (HGET, HMSET, EXPIRE) never carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR in this window; they simply stop being emitted, so there is no evidence that valkey returned command-level errors — the failure observed is at connection establishment.

frontend-proxy itself stayed Running/Ready with 0 restarts, its egress spans to frontend are 15 s long with http.status_code 0, and the innermost failing spans belong to cart — the 504 is a timeout on a slow upstream, not a proxy crash.

rejected_hypothesis.text: Rejected: that valkey-cart was OOM-killed or restarted and thereby broke cart storage. Its container has restartCount 0, empty lastState, memory failcnt 0 and was still exporting Redis metrics at 17:02:18Z.

Rejected as this cause: the stuck old pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s.
